clue.text: Slash rank when caught in small offence

indicators.note: something caught in a net sits inside it, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: S is small; sus was the old British offence of loitering as a suspected person
olid is a rare word for rank or foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A demotion handed out after someone is caught committing a minor offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The sus law let British police stop people merely suspected of intending a crime. Olid, meaning stinking, is a dictionary word that crosswords love.
explanation.definitionFit: A solidus is the printed oblique stroke, another name for the forward slash character.

clue.text: Gas and benzene finally swell and ignite

indicators.note: finally points at the end of each of the two words before it

blocks.note: the closing letter of each word
a swell is a well-dressed gent, a toff

explanation.surface: Fuel vapour and a hydrocarbon expand and catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Finally covers both gas and benzene. Swell and toff are both old British words for a posh, smartly dressed man.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a firework or charge is to ignite it, making it go off.

clue.text: Baltic salad drunkenly called for

indicators.note: an order spoken by a slurring customer comes out sounding different

blocks.note: the salad leaf as a tipsy diner might pronounce it

explanation.surface: A diner from the Baltic orders a salad after too many drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is loose on purpose: the slurred speech excuses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettish is an old name for Latvian, the language and people of a Baltic state.

clue.text: Missed tea, settled for a small coffee

indicators.note: letters that have settled have come to rest in a new arrangement

blocks.note: all nine letters are used

explanation.surface: Having missed out on tea, someone makes do with an espresso.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup of strong black coffee, or the little cup itself; the French means half-cup.

clue.text: Reveals hat, a sensation

blocks.note: to reveal is to show
a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Someone unveils a hat that causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A showstopper is a performance or item so striking that it halts proceedings with applause.

clue.text: Occasional worker takes time to paint

blocks.note: a temp works for short spells as needed
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A casual worker is slow to get on with decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a type of paint made by binding pigment with egg yolk, used by early painters.

clue.text: A fixture? I'd say not

indicators.note: what I would say is the word spoken, so its sound counts, not its spelling

blocks.note: first meaning: a cup match on the sports calendar
second meaning: the spoken word matches one for a fastening, a synonym of the answer

explanation.surface: Someone doubts whether an event is really on the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Not looks like a flat denial; spoken, it is knot, which is another word for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup tie is a scheduled match in a knockout competition; a knot is something tied.

clue.text: Comics, including posh Wizard

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: comics are magazines, mags
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U speech

explanation.surface: A set of comic books featuring an upper-class sorcerer.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a magician or sorcerer, like the Magi of the Nativity story.

clue.text: Looks on foreign money as something hideous

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the parts follow one another

blocks.note: to eye is to look at
the öre is a Scandinavian coin

explanation.surface: Someone eyes foreign banknotes with disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly sight, typically a building that spoils the view.

clue.text: Tacitus was a deep thinker, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the sound matters

blocks.note: an analyst examines things in depth

explanation.surface: The Roman historian is said to have been a profound thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus wrote the Annals, a year-by-year history of Rome, which makes him a chronicler of yearly records.

clue.text: Ritual post to the archbishop is empty

blocks.note: taken as written
William Temple was Archbishop of Canterbury
O, zero, is what an empty thing contains

explanation.surface: A senior churchman's role is said to be a hollow position.
explanation.walkthrough: The archbishop is a famous name, Temple, and he has the empty O inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem pole is a carved wooden column set up by Pacific Northwest peoples, bearing clan emblems with ceremonial meaning.

clue.text: Vigorous little general is shown round the corps

indicators.note: one part is displayed wrapped around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: Gen is the short form of general
the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A short but energetic army general is given a tour of his unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Little general means its abbreviation, not a short officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Green can describe something fresh, youthful and flourishing, as in a green old age.

clue.text: Old county captain

blocks.note: first meaning: the former Welsh county, Flintshire, named after its town
second meaning: the pirate captain in Treasure Island, whose parrot repeats his name

explanation.surface: An officer from a former shire.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a historic Welsh county abolished in 1974 and to Stevenson's dead pirate commander.

clue.text: European gets loaf and comes round for tea

blocks.note: a person from Switzerland
a roll is a small individual loaf

explanation.surface: A visitor from the continent picks up bread and drops by for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the cake itself: it is rolled round in a spiral and served at teatime.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a sponge cake spread with jam and rolled into a cylinder, a teatime classic.

clue.text: Islanders one's met among people from the subcontinent

indicators.note: being met among a crowd means standing in the middle of it

blocks.note: people from India
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Islanders meet up with someone among a group of South Asians.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is an archipelago of thousands of islands, so its people are islanders.

clue.text: The farce's words caused trouble — it's set in the bedroom

indicators.note: words that cause trouble are thrown into disorder, so their letters are jumbled

blocks.note: all fourteen letters are used

explanation.surface: A bedroom farce in which the script itself is the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedroom farces are set in bedrooms; here the set is the furniture on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest of drawers is a standard piece of bedroom furniture for storing clothes.

clue.text: States things in camera when ordered; take note

indicators.note: being ordered means being put into a new sequence

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: A court hears things privately, under orders.
explanation.walkthrough: States looks like a verb; it is the United States. In camera is legal Latin for a private hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Americana are objects and artefacts typical of the United States and its culture.

clue.text: Palm a high card: officer and boy are taken in

indicators.note: things taken in are absorbed inside, so they go within another part

blocks.note: the ace is the top card in many games
CO is commanding officer
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A card cheat conceals an ace while an officer and a lad are fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: Palm looks like the cheat's move; it is a prize, as in bearing the palm.
explanation.definitionFit: The palm was a victor's emblem of honour, so both words mean an award or tribute.

clue.text: Letters that show similarity

blocks.note: first meaning: written messages exchanged between people
second meaning: a close match or agreement between two things

explanation.surface: Messages that reveal how alike two people are.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both mail exchanged by writers and the matching of one thing with another.

clue.text: I learnt to dance the sailor's step

indicators.note: dancing letters jump about and land in another order

blocks.note: all seven letters are used

explanation.surface: Someone learnt the hornpipe, the dance step of seafarers.
explanation.walkthrough: Step looks like a dance move; it is a rung to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are small ropes tied across a ship's shrouds to form ladder rungs for climbing the rigging.

clue.text: The Bellman's mistake?

blocks.note: surface: an error by the town crier, or by the Bellman of Lewis Carroll's Snark
setter's reading: a man ringing bells produces a loud ringing noise, and the same word is slang for a blunder

explanation.walkthrough: To drop a clanger is British slang for making an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A clanger is a conspicuous blunder, and also something that clangs like a bell.

clue.text: Take out chronicler of gypsy life

blocks.note: first meaning: to take out a library book or a loan
second meaning: George ..., the Victorian author of Lavengro and The Romany Rye

explanation.surface: Remove the writer who recorded the lives of travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to use something on loan, and George Borrow wrote books about wandering Romany people.

clue.text: Part of town that's unfashionable; don't pass through, son

definitions.note: the answer is plural; the outer districts of a town

blocks.note: out of fashion
to skirt a place is to go round its edge
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Directions to a son: the shabby district is to be avoided, go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Outskirts are the outlying edges of a town, away from its centre.

clue.text: Snake - it was found under vessel when picked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads from the bottom
in a down clue one part sitting under another follows it

blocks.note: Noah's vessel
taken as written

explanation.surface: A serpent discovered beneath a boat as it was lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Picked up suggests a sound clue, but here it lifts the vessel upward in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: The krait is a highly venomous South Asian snake, related to cobras.

clue.text: See in him a good example of perfection

indicators.note: the solver is told to look inside the following words to spot the answer

blocks.note: running across the three words

explanation.surface: Praise for a man held up as a model of the ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final adult stage of an insect, traditionally called its perfect form.

clue.text: Femininity personified, but the creature is finally skint

indicators.note: skint means broke, so the word loses what comes at its end

blocks.note: a creature is an animal

explanation.surface: Womanliness in human form, yet the being is penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jung's psychology the anima is the feminine side within a man, imagined as an inner female figure.

clue.text: Square cape

blocks.note: first meaning: the London square with Nelson's Column
second meaning: the Spanish headland off which Nelson won in 1805

explanation.definitionFit: The name is shared by a famous central London plaza and a Spanish coastal headland, linked through Nelson's victory.

clue.text: One at sea in desert rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upward, from the bottom

blocks.note: to rat is to desert, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A sailor in the desert as the sun comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar, short for tarpaulin, is old slang for a seaman or sailor.

clue.text: Saxon ruler found in booth

blocks.note: first meaning: a prince of Saxony, one of those who chose the Holy Roman Emperor
second meaning: a voter, found in a polling booth

explanation.surface: A German monarch discovered hiding in a kiosk.
explanation.definitionFit: The rulers of Saxony held the title because they voted for the emperor; anyone casting a ballot holds it too.

clue.text: Bird — the odds are against one flying straight

indicators.note: being against means sitting right next to, so the parts are placed side by side

blocks.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the off
an arrow flies straight

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's view that a bird is unlikely to fly in a straight line.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price, is a horse-racing term for the final odds.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird, common in gardens and towns.
